question: As of April 07, 2025, what is the total value of MSCI's operating leases (in $'s, thousands) that are maturing in the next three years? What percentage?
model_answer:
Using MSCI's 10-K for fiscal year 2024, the most recent annual lease table before April 7, 2025, about **$85,002 thousand** (roughly $85.0 million) of operating lease payments fall due in the next three years. That is about **51.3%** of total payments.

The table shows undiscounted payments as of December 31, 2024. The three years are 2025, 2026 and 2027.

| Year | Operating lease payments ($ thousands) |
|---|---|
| 2025 | 30,220 |
| 2026 | 30,361 |
| 2027 | 24,421 |
| **Three-year total** | **85,002** |

Total undiscounted operating lease payments are $165,605 thousand. The percentage is 85,002 ÷ 165,605 ≈ 51.3%.

On a present-value basis, total operating lease liabilities are $146,004 thousand. That figure isn't broken out by year. Measured against it, the same $85,002 thousand would be about 58.2%, but that mixes undiscounted and discounted amounts, so I used the undiscounted total.

Source: [MSCI Form 10-K FY2024](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1408198/000140819825000053/msci-20241231.htm)
judge_reason: Correct three-year total ($85,002K) and percentage (51.3%); the alternative 58.2% figure is noted but explicitly not adopted.
